text_blocks.snippet: Securing large language models (LLMs) requires applying defense-in-depth across inputs, outputs, data pipelines, and agentic workflows to mitigate risks like prompt injection and data leakage.
snippet_highlighted_words: applying defense-in-depth across inputs, outputs, data pipelines, and agentic workflows

list.snippet: Sanitize and Filter Inputs: Constrain and inspect all incoming user prompts, system context, and retrieved documents to block direct or indirect prompt injections. Use allow-lists and strip hidden control characters.

Validate and Handle Outputs Safely: Treat all model-generated text, code, or tool commands as untrusted data. Apply schema validation, content filters, and execution sandboxing before displaying or running outputs.

Enforce Least Privilege and Zero Trust: Limit agentic tools, API integrations, and user permissions to only what is strictly necessary for the specific task. Implement human-in-the-loop controls for high-risk autonomous actions.
Implement AI Security Gateways: Deploy specialized AI Security Gateways as intermediaries to monitor traffic, enforce rate limits, handle authentication, and block malicious payloads in real time.

Practice Data Minimization and Governance: Restrict training, fine-tuning, and RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) inputs to non-sensitive data, maintain strict dataset lineage, and audit repositories regularly.

Conduct Continuous Red Teaming: Test your LLM applications against the OWASP Top 10 for LLMs using automated frameworks and penetration testing to discover structural vulnerabilities before deployment.
